item: a Quick build orders its scans by this machine's own times and names each figure's source
summary: Field test 2026-11-14 row 74 (report 9): the card audit sat at 60.5 s in the field-median table and took about 300 s on that machine (302 s on the 2026-11-07 Windows run), so a Quick build ran it fourth and it spent half the 600 s scan budget the scans after it were planned to have. The machine's own scan times were already kept after every build (diagnostics.scan_walls.v1) but only fed the Thorough estimate. diagnostics_plan.machine_table now gives every scan's cost on this machine (its last wall time scaled by the mention rows now against then, never above its 300 s deadline; the field median for a scan not yet timed here, or when the store cannot be read) and the build orders its scans, writes est_s on each entry and states the skipped reason by that table; the manifest's planned list carries est_from (this-machine or field-median) per scan. For ORDERING a figure here below the field median is not used (one cheap run is not the next one's cost: leads-quality is 0.01 s from a fresh Home feed and up to 240 s without one), while the Thorough estimate sums the figures as measured; a damaged stored figure is no figure, never a failed build; a scan that finished under a deadline the budget shortened is now remembered, so a scan Quick runs late can be timed lower. The estimate is made honest rather than the audit made quicker: the audit's cost is the producer pass on the corpus, which the budget already bounds. Row 10 (heavy.statement_budget) was found already done on main.
